examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating Combinations Given Using Alternate Notation
examples.worked_solution:
First, note that $\displaystyle{{12}\choose{10}}$ means the same thing as $_{12}C_{10}.$

 In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_nC_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=12$ and $r=10,$ we get

$$
\require{cancel}
	\eqalign{
                            _{12}C_{10} &= \dfrac {12!} {(12 - 10)!10!} \[5pt]
                            &= \dfrac {12!} {2!10!} \[5pt]
                            &= \dfrac {12 \cdot 11 \cdot \cancel{10!}} {2!\cdot\cancel{10!}} \[5pt]
                            &= \dfrac {12 \cdot 11} {2} \[5pt]
 	                            &= 66.
	}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=15$ and $r=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{15}{C}_{0} & =\frac{15!}{(15-0)!\,0!} \\  & =\frac{15!}{15!\,0!} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{15!}}{\cancel{15!}\cdot 1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
